# 1 Enoch Chapter 75 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**75:1** The leaders of the heads of the thousands who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars are also concerned with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office according to the reckoning of the year; and these serve on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.

**75:2** And because of them people go wrong therein; for those luminaries truly render service on the world-stations, one in the first portal, one in the third portal of heaven, one in the fourth portal, and one in the sixth portal, and the exactness of the year is accomplished through its three hundred and sixty-four stations.

**75:3** For the signs and the times and the years and the days, the angel Uriel showed me — he whom the Lord of glory has set forever over all the luminaries of heaven and in the world, that they should rule on the face of heaven and be seen on the earth, and serve as leaders for day and night: the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the ministering creatures who revolve in all the chariots of heaven.

**75:4** In like manner Uriel showed me twelve portals open in the circuit of the sun's chariot in heaven, through which the rays of the sun break forth; and from them warmth is diffused over the earth when they are opened at their appointed seasons.

**75:5** And for the winds, and the spirit of the dew, and of the cloud, and of the mist which rests over the earth and dwells in it —

**75:6** in like manner the spirit of the rain and the dew, when it descends from that dwelling; and in all these the pattern of their course is the same in winter and in summer.

**75:7** And I saw twelve portals open in heaven, from which issue forth the winds, and from which the dew and rain and mist and frost and snow and hail pour down upon the earth.

**75:8** In seven of these portals were two and a half portions of cold, and in five of them were portions bringing warmth and cold and dew and rain and winds and storms.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering adjudicated from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. The four intercalary days (v. 1-2) are placed at the transitions between the four seasons in the 364-day calendar — falling on the days after days 91, 182, 273, and 364. They mark the solstices and equinoxes. Uriel (v. 3) is the supreme angelic administrator of all celestial phenomena. The twelve solar portals (v. 4) and twelve wind portals (v. 7) create a comprehensive cosmological grid.*
